message: Reviewed from dated primary evidence using the Codex subscription.

data.headline: SPY: the curve steepened by two basis points.
data.summary: The difference between US ten- and two-year Treasury yields widened from 32 to 34 basis points between November 2 and 3. Both yields rose. That detail matters: a steeper curve driven by higher long yields does not give every S&P 500 company the same financing or valuation benefit.

bull.text: The two-year yield rose only 2 basis points to 4.61%, versus a 4-basis-point rise in the ten-year to 4.95%. The longer benchmark rose more; this spread is useful context for comparing lenders with companies that borrow.

bear.text: At 4.95%, the ten-year yield was higher than the previous 4.91%. All else equal, a higher discount rate reduces the present value of future earnings. The figures do not show what happened to index earnings or prices.

watch.text: October 27 S&P futures showed asset managers net long 923,449 contracts and leveraged funds net short 400,604. The groups were on opposite sides before these yield observations.

limitations: The curve is measured from Treasury yields, not S&P 500 share prices. Futures category positions are weekly and do not measure SPY creations, redemptions or present investor intent.
The available evidence does not support a calibrated forecast or a directional trading call.
